$comment: What makes the manual roster a ratchet instead of a wish.
WHY A RATCHET AND NOT A FLAT RULE. Every item in scripts/manual-test-roster.mjs
is meant to gate the ship. The roster measures 882 rows and 163.7 hours, which
is roughly twenty working days for one maintainer. Making all of it blocking on
day one would produce a gate nobody can walk, and a gate nobody can walk gets
bulk-overridden, which is worse than no gate: it teaches the override to mean
nothing. The `e2e` CI step is the worked example already in this repository. It
carries `failure: ignore`, so it is not a gate, and v0.4 shipped without the
suite ever running with nothing recording that fact.
So the gate starts at what is walkable and WIDENS, and the pair below is what
makes widening the only direction available.
gatedTiers, gatedClients  MAY ONLY GROW. Together they are the POLICY: which
tiers block, on which clients. Set inclusion is checked
against RATCHET_BASELINE in scripts/check-manual-test-roster.mjs,
so narrowing the gate takes an edit to two files with two
different rationales, one of which is code under review.
totalMinutesCeiling TRACKS THE ROSTER. It is how much manual work the roster
asks for in total. `--record` moves it DOWN only, so paying
automation debt is the one way the tooling can change it. A
RAISE is a hand edit that carries its argument beside the two
already in this file. The direction is NOT machine-enforced,
and deliberately so: a ceiling that could only fall would mean
a genuinely new surface needing a human could never be gated,
which is the opposite of what this ratchet is for. What IS
enforced is that the roster fits the ceiling, so a raise is
the only way to add manual work and it cannot be silent.
totalMinutesCeiling MAY ONLY FALL BY ITSELF. It is how much manual work the
roster asks for in total. It falls when automation debt is
paid and a manual item moves into e2e/. Its rising means
somebody added manual work instead of automating it, and
that is an argument somebody makes in a PR rather than a
silent edit.
"By itself" is the load-bearing half and this line said
only "MAY ONLY FALL" until myne-md/myne#609, which is why
two reviewers read the raise below as a rule being broken
and had to reconstruct the exception from the guard's own
failure message. The message is what the rule actually is:
"raise the ceiling in the same change and say what added
it". `--record` moves it DOWNWARD only; upward is a hand
edit that lands in git with a written argument beside it,
which is the same shape as widening `gatedTiers`. A rule
whose real exception lives only in an error string is a
rule the next author re-litigates.
WHY THE GATE IS A POLICY AND NOT A MINUTE COUNT. The first shape bounded gating
MINUTES with a floor that could only rise, and it argued against the one move
this system exists to encourage. An author who writes an e2e scenario covering a
core item and deletes the item drops the gating minute count, so the guard called
that 'the gate NARROWED' and told them the remedy was the edit it calls never
legitimate. A ratio fails identically, because automating a core item leaves the
numerator and the denominator together. Sets are what 'the gate widens' means.
EITHER HALF ALONE IS GAMEABLE, which is why both are here. A policy alone is
satisfied by adding cheap manual items inside it; a ceiling alone is satisfied by
deleting items nobody wanted to run. Together they say: the share of the roster
that blocks goes up, and the roster itself goes down.
gatedMinutes IS THE THIRD NUMBER, and it exists because the two above bound
THIS FILE and not the roster's composition. Retiering a core
item to standard satisfies both and moves neither: gating
minutes fall, total minutes do not. Dropping a gated client
from an item is worse, because total falls too, --record is
then invited, and the smaller ceiling locks in as progress.
So the guard compares the two DROPS: gating may not fall by
more than total does. Automating an item moves both together
by construction, so the rule cannot punish the one move this
whole system exists to encourage. Found by the myne-bot
review of PR #576, which measured this comment against the
code and found the comment claiming the larger property.
MEASURED 2026-08-22 against the roster as it stands (myne-md/myne#548):
882 rows and 9822 minutes in total, of which 243 rows and 3533 minutes gate.
That is 36.0% of the roster blocking today.
A row is one observation on one client; estimateMin is one execution on one
client, so an item naming three clients is three sittings.
265 further observations were refuted into automation debt before this
measurement: an e2e scenario could honestly assert them, so they are not
manual items at all. Paying that debt is what moves the ceiling down.

CEILING RAISED 9822 -> 10098 for the vault-import feature (myne-md/myne#464),
in the sanctioned direction: a new surface that genuinely needs a human. What
added the minutes, named so the raise is an argument rather than a number:
+ the two-timer interaction, and it is the reason this entry exists at all.
`import_set_hold` DEFERS idle auto-lock for the length of an import, and a
30-minute source-slot TTL, deliberately INDEPENDENT of that hold, is what
bounds the window in which two vaults' keys are resident (threat-model.md
A6). Both are measured in real minutes. A scenario lives for seconds and
would have to fake both clocks, and a faked clock stops proving the exact
coupling the design was worried about. 45 minutes on three clients.
+ the recovery-phrase path leaving the SOURCE vault unchanged. The property
is an absence in a vault the scenario has finished with: that its
vault.meta was not rewritten. Checking it means unlocking that vault again
with its ORIGINAL password, which is a second full Argon2id derivation
against a vault the harness has already torn down. decisions 0542 rests on
this being true, so it is gated rather than assumed.
+ the memory ceiling on a real import. The design holds one note body and
one attachment in RAM at a time; the seeded fixture is six notes and two
small attachments, so the harness makes no observation that could refute
it.
+ whether a squiggle actually disappears. The dictionary carry is covered by
two unit tiers, but the E2E fixture deliberately writes no
vault.dictionary: the generator cannot seal one without keeping a second
copy of the postcard payload that lives in src-tauri/src/spell/, and a
fixture that re-implements a format drifts from it silently. What a human
checks here is the rendering neither unit tier reaches.
CEILING RAISED 9822 -> 9842 by myne-md/myne#508, in the sanctioned direction.
What added the twenty minutes:

WHY THESE GATED CLIENTS: every client this release ships, and only that.
desktop-windows is the sole exclusion, because Windows is not shipped
(myne#178 defers it). Its roster entries stay, because a recorded decision is
not the same as an omission, and they gate the release that ships Windows.
An earlier version of this file also excluded cli and clipper, on the stated
grounds that 'neither carries a core-tier item today'. That was FALSE for
clipper, which carries five core items and 69 minutes, among them clipping
with the vault LOCKED and three pairing-rejection items: exactly the security
boundaries a gate is for. It was also not a policy but a measurement, so the
day somebody added a core CLI item the client would have started gating for a
reason nobody decided. Recorded here rather than quietly corrected, because a
footnote that does not describe its own file is the failure mode this whole
roster exists to catch.
cli carries zero core minutes today and is on the list anyway. That is the
point: it gates the moment a core CLI item is written, which is the right
behaviour for a door that opens an unlocked vault to a second OS process.
CEILING RAISED 9822 -> 9828 by myne-md/myne#642 AND THEN REVERTED, which is
worth keeping because the raise was argued and was still wrong. The six
minutes were a macOS item for the command socket's blocking-first-read

accepted stream itself and fail on every Unix including the Linux container

can honestly judge it, it is not a manual item, it is a scenario you owe. The
reason named a real mechanism and was simply wrong about it, which the
guard's phrase denylist cannot catch, so the correction lives here.

$comment2: CEILING RAISED 9822 -> 9846 by myne-md/myne#456, in the sanctioned direction.
What added the minutes, named so the raise is an argument:
+ the disclosure-recall item now runs on ios and android as well. That item
is the reversal of a stated anti-feature and it measures a human reader's
recall, so the client list is the list of surfaces on which a person can
read the screen. #456 ships the consent screen on the phone, and its
clauses are the same strings as the desktop ones BY CONSTRUCTION, since
both import them from @myne/copy. What is not shared is the geometry:
seven clauses do not fit on a phone, so the phone is the surface where a
reader can finish without having reached the clause that matters, and
that is a thing only a person can be observed doing. 12 minutes on each
of the two new clients, which is the whole of 9822 -> 9846.
CEILING RAISED 9846 -> 9878 by the same issue, one task later. What added
the minutes:
+ the LIVE cost line on a phone, 10 minutes on ios and android, core. The
figures are what docs/decisions/ai/0515 rests the remote arm's lack of a
volume bound on, and agentStart returns only when the loop has STOPPED,
so a surface reading them off the reply discloses nothing at all for a
run that was cancelled or that died with the foreground. That the
figures advance mid-run IS asserted, in
mobile/tests/components/AiChatFlow.test.tsx against a held-open reply,
so the item is scoped to the half no lane reaches: the phone leaving the
foreground, which is an OS memory-pressure decision about a real process
and decides whether the reply ever arrives at all.
+ the five-column bottom bar, 6 minutes on ios and android, standard. Text
width at 10px is a property of that OS version's font stack; jsdom
computes no layout and the flow tier is Chromium rather than WKWebView
or Android WebView. The containment (ellipsis, minWidth:0) is asserted
in mobile/tests/components/TabBar.test.tsx, so what is left for a person
is whether a truncated label is still readable.
CEILING RAISED 9878 -> 9902 by the same issue, task 11. What added the
minutes:
+ the scope disclosure READ ON A PHONE, 12 minutes on ios and android,
core. The failure it looks for is a fact pushed off-screen, and on a
phone what pushes it is the software keyboard, whose height the OS, the
active input method and the user's own settings decide between them. No
lane raises one: jsdom computes no layout and the Playwright flow tier
drives Chromium in a fixed viewport with no keyboard at all. That every
fact is PRESENT is asserted in
mobile/tests/components/AiScopeSheet.test.tsx, so the item is scoped to
whether a person can read them at the moment they must decide, which is
the whole of what makes this screen a gate rather than a notice.
CEILING RAISED 9902 -> 9930 by the same issue, task 12. What added the
minutes:
+ the agent REVIEW read on a real phone, 14 minutes on ios and android,
core. Two halves, each out of reach for its own reason. Whether a diff
is READABLE at 390px is a judgement about a person's comprehension, and
the item's pass condition is written as a question to answer honestly
rather than as an assertion, because the failure mode is a user tapping
Apply since reading was worse than trusting. And the back gesture is a
real OS gesture: Android's hardware button and iOS's edge-swipe are
system events no lane raises, and the flow tier drives Chromium in a
desktop browser with neither. That the screen CLAIMS a history entry
and a replacement after each pop is asserted in
mobile/tests/components/AiReviewFlow.test.tsx.
CEILING RAISED 9930 -> 9950 by the same issue, task 13. What added the
minutes:
+ the one-tap undo's DISAPPEARANCE, 10 minutes on ios and android, core.
The record holds verbatim note plaintext and is deliberately not
persisted, because writing it to disk would reverse the argument
docs/decisions/ai/0515 rests on; snapshot metadata records no origin, so
it cannot be rebuilt afterwards either. The limit is therefore stated
rather than fixed, and what a person checks is that the offer really is
gone AND the durable path really is populated, on the same device, in
that order. What makes the offer go is the OS reclaiming a backgrounded
process, a memory-pressure judgement about real hardware that no
simulator, container or flow tier reproduces.
CEILING RAISED 10511 -> 10527 by myne-md/myne#684, in the sanctioned
direction. What added the minutes, named so the raise is an argument:

NOTHING WAS SUBTRACTED, and one item that could have been is worth naming.
The second-device item under settings.block.ai-provider was written against
the SYNC-22 residual: consent was vault content, so it synced, and a newly
enrolled device began sending with nobody at it having seen the screen. #456
made ai_provider_consent device-local, which removes the residual, and the
tempting move was to delete the item as fixed. It was rewritten instead, at
the same 30 minutes and the same clients: the remedy is an ABSENCE of packets
from a device nobody has touched, a client that showed the screen and sent
anyway would look identical on screen, and a capture across two enrolled
devices is the only place that difference is visible. Deleting an item
because the code now claims to be right is how a gate stops checking the
thing it was built for.
CEILING RAISED 10511 -> 10555 by myne-md/myne#675, task 14. What added the
minutes:
+ the conversation-history surface on the two desktop WebViews this lane
never drives, 10 minutes on desktop-macos and desktop-windows, core.
The automated desktop scenario runs WebKitGTK in a Linux container, so

release now waits on a human having opened history on macOS/Windows and on
both phone platforms. That is the point of the raise rather than its cost:
a persisted-conversation feature whose only human eyes were ever on Linux
and Chromium would ship its delete-everywhere and lock-continue promises
unobserved on four of its six clients.
